origin.description: A short name for the type. Types that commonly appear in a data frame stay within four characters. Most inputs are forwarded to vctrs::vec_ptype_abbr().

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An object to summarise. Methods are in place for atomic vectors and the usual variants.

origin.details: The shared manual page examples obj_sum and size_sum, which have their own files. These lines print type_sum. An unordered factor is fct, with no shape suffix. An ordered factor is ord. A data frame drops the first dimension, so one column is df[,1]. A 2 by 2 integer matrix is int[,2]. Titanic is table[,2,2,2]. A function is fn, an environment is env, and NULL is NULL. When a pillar is formatted, type_sum sees a slice of the column, and the text should depend on the type rather than the values.
origin.example:
type_sum(factor(letters[1:3]))
type_sum(ordered(letters[1:3]))
type_sum(1:10)
type_sum(matrix(1:4, nrow = 2))
type_sum(Titanic)
type_sum(data.frame(a = 1))
type_sum(Sys.Date())
type_sum(Sys.time())
type_sum(list(1, 2))
type_sum(mean)
type_sum(NULL)

translation.description: The same short names. An unordered Factor is fct. An ordered Factor is ord. Other vectors use vec_ptype_abbr with the shape suffix.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A vector, Factor, Matrix, DataFrame, Table, List, date, datetime, function, Environment, or NULL. A bare list is an atomic vector. An R list is List.

translation.details: Integer is int, double is dbl, logical is lgl, character is chr, complex is cpl, and raw is raw. One column is df[,1]. matrix(1:4, nrow = 2) is int[,2]. Titanic's dimensions are table[,2,2,2]. Date is date and POSIXct is dttm. A function is fn, Environment() is env, and NULL is NULL. A one-dimensional dim of length 1 is int[1d]. A complex scalar is summarised as cpl even though vec_is currently rejects it.
translation.example:
from datetime import date, datetime

from cli._options import options as cli_options

cli_options(**{"cli.unicode": True})

from pillar._vec import NULL, DataFrame, Factor, List, Matrix, Table
from pillar.summary import type_sum


def mean(values):
    return values


print(type_sum(Factor(["a", "b", "c"])))
print(type_sum(Factor(["a", "b", "c"], ordered=True)))
print(type_sum(list(range(1, 11))))
print(type_sum(Matrix(list(range(1, 5)), 2)))
print(type_sum(Table((4, 2, 2, 2))))
print(type_sum(DataFrame({"a": [1]})))
print(type_sum(date.today()))
print(type_sum(datetime.now()))
print(type_sum(List([1, 2])))
print(type_sum(mean))
print(type_sum(NULL))
